notes: §1985:VI.5.15.3 SR2: 'A signed numeric literal must have associated with it a signed numeric PICTURE character-string.' Every VALUE literal of an item, a table element, a report-section entry and each literal and THRU end of a condition-name passes ScreenValueLiteral, whose ValidateNumericValue refuses a signed literal on an unsigned subject (COBOL1625); a numeric-edited subject takes no numeric literal at 85 (§1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b; ScreenNumericEditedNumericLiteral, COBOL0900, accepted at 2023); and the escape of the prior PARTIAL (a group conditional variable, PB5215 landed) is closed by CheckValueLiteralClassesPass.ScreenGroupConditionName, which sends a group's 88 literals through ValidateValueCategory (COBOL1657). Probed at --std 85: (d) refused: -1 and +1 on PIC 99, -0 on PIC 99 COMP, 88 VALUE -1 and 88 VALUE 1 THRU +5 on PIC 99, 88 VALUE -1 under an alphanumeric group and +1 under a REDEFINES group, -1 on PIC X(2), -1 on PIC 99 OCCURS 3, -1 on a report-section PIC 99 COLUMN entry, -1 on PIC -99 (item and 88, COBOL0900; accepted at --std 2023); accepted: -1 and +1 on S99, -1.5 on S9V9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE, -12 on S99 COMP, 88 -5 THRU -1 on S99, -1 on a report-section S99 entry. Classes a, e, f do not reach this rule. The witness is the refusal of a signed literal on an unsigned item. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5215 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5215 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-05.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-05-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985 requires 'a signed numeric PICTURE character-string' for a signed numeric literal, and §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b gives numeric edited items nonnumeric literals only. §2023:13.18.63.3 SR3 admits 'either a signed numeric data item or a numeric-edited data item with a representation of a sign', and §2023:13.18.63.3 SR6 lets numeric literals initialize numeric-edited items 'such that no truncation of digits or sign is required'. A signed literal for a numeric-edited item, refused in 1985, is accepted. SR3 is an all-formats rule, so it also governs condition-name values. Both editions refuse at compile time.
